Protecting cultural heritage is the responsibility of every citizen.
Protect cultural heritages is every citizen's duty.
It is every citizen responsible to protect cultural heritage.
The protection of cultural heritage is responsible for every citizen.
动名词作主语、heritage 为不可数名词；第二项动词原形作主语且 heritages 错误，第三项词性错误，第四项意为“保护对公民负责”，逻辑错误。
由于缺乏经验，他在工作中犯了不少错误。
Owing to his lack of experience, he made quite a few mistakes at work.
Owing to his lack of experience, he made few mistakes at work.
Due to lack experience, he made a few mistakes in work.
Because he lacked of experience, he did many mistakes at work.
quite a few 意为“相当多”；few 意为“几乎没有”，意思相反；lack 作动词不加 of，make mistakes 不用 do。
饺子象征着团圆和好运。
Dumplings symbolize reunion and good fortune.
Dumplings are symbolized reunion and good luck.
Dumplings symbol family gather and good luck.
Dumplings stand for reunite and lucky.
symbolize 是及物动词，直接接名词；第二项被动误用，symbol 是名词，reunite、lucky 词性错误。
我们必须采取有效措施来应对气候变化。
We must take effective measures to cope with climate change.
We must take efficient measure to deal climate change.
We must adopt effective measures to response climate change.
Effective measures must take to tackle climate change.
take measures to cope with 是地道搭配；measure 应为复数且 deal 后缺 with，response 是名词，第四项应为被动 must be taken。
毫无疑问，阅读能够开阔我们的视野。
There is no doubt that reading can broaden our horizons.
There is no doubt whether reading can broaden our horizons.
Without doubt, reading can open our eyesight wide.
No doubt that reading can widen our visual field.
There is no doubt that ... 用于肯定句，broaden one's horizons 是固定搭配；whether 用于否定性怀疑不当，eyesight、visual field 是字面直译。
这家博物馆每年吸引数百万游客。
The museum attracts millions of visitors every year.
The museum attracts millions visitors every year.
The museum attracts several millions of visitors each year.
The museum is attracted by millions of tourists every year.
表示“数百万”用 millions of；millions 后缺 of，several millions of 不规范（应为 several million），第四项被动语态使意思颠倒。

A. Dockless shared bicycles spread rapidly across Chinese cities around 2016, backed by billions of dollars in venture capital.
B. Within two years, oversupply led to mountains of abandoned bikes piling up on sidewalks and in vacant lots.
C. Several operators collapsed, and many users struggled to recover the deposits they had paid.
D. Today the industry is smaller but more tightly regulated, with cities setting caps on fleet sizes.◆Some customers found it hard to get their money back after companies went out of business.
C 段提到运营商倒闭后许多用户难以拿回押金，与“公司倒闭后顾客难以要回钱”对应。

A. Cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island.

D 段说把屋顶刷白、种行道树是最便宜的降温方法，与“低成本措施可降温”对应。

C 段 personalized playlists 对应 tailored music selections，calmer and less agitated 对应 reduce restlessness。

A. Roughly a third of all food produced worldwide is lost or wasted somewhere between the farm and the dinner table.

D. Some ecologists caution that planting trees in arid regions can deplete groundwater if species are poorly chosen.◆Planting trees in dry areas may harm water supplies if it is not done properly.
D 段说在干旱地区若树种选择不当会耗尽地下水，与题干对应。

B 段说五十多个国家专门推出签证吸引数字游民，与题干对应。

C 段说自由玩耍让孩子学会协商规则、管控风险、自行解决冲突，即社交与解决问题的能力。

Placebos—sugar pills with no active ingredients—have long served as a baseline against which real drugs are measured. Surprisingly, recent trials have found that placebos can relieve symptoms even when patients are told openly that the pills are fake. Researchers suspect that the ritual of treatment, such as visiting a caring doctor and taking pills at regular times, triggers the body's own pain-relieving mechanisms. Still, they caution that placebos cannot shrink tumors or cure infections; their effects are largely confined to subjective symptoms such as pain and fatigue.◆What is surprising about the recent trials?
Placebos worked even when patients knew they were inactive.
Placebos proved more effective than real drugs.
Patients refused to take pills without active ingredients.
Doctors could not tell placebos from real drugs.
第二句说即使明确告知病人药是假的，安慰剂仍能缓解症状；其余选项文中均未提及。

A growing body of evidence links access to green space with better mental health. In one large study, city residents who lived within walking distance of a park reported lower levels of anxiety, even after researchers controlled for income and age. The benefits appear to depend less on the size of a green space than on how often people actually use it. Urban planners are therefore being urged to scatter small 'pocket parks' throughout neighborhoods rather than concentrate resources on a single large park on the city's edge.◆Why did the researchers control for income and age?
To rule out other factors that might explain the lower anxiety.
To show that wealthy residents visit parks more often.
To prove that older people need more green space.
To compare mental health across different cities.
控制收入和年龄是为了排除其他可能的解释因素，确保焦虑降低与公园有关；其余选项为无中生有。

The gig economy promises workers flexibility: drivers and couriers can, in theory, log on and off whenever they like. In practice, however, many find that the algorithms assigning tasks reward those who accept every order and penalize those who decline. As a result, the freedom advertised by platforms is often more apparent than real. Some governments have responded by requiring platforms to provide basic insurance and to explain how their algorithms rank workers.◆What does the author mean by saying the freedom is "more apparent than real"?
Workers' flexibility is limited in reality despite appearances.
Workers enjoy more freedom than they realize.
Platforms openly admit that workers have no freedom.
Only experienced drivers can enjoy real freedom.
前文说算法惩罚拒单者，因此所谓自由只是表面的，实际上受到限制。

Nostalgia was once classified as a medical disorder, a form of homesickness believed to afflict soldiers and sailors far from home. Modern psychologists take a far kinder view. Experiments show that recalling fond memories can strengthen people's sense of meaning in life and make them feel more connected to others. Nostalgia seems especially common during periods of loneliness or transition, suggesting that it may serve as a psychological resource rather than a sign of weakness.◆How has the view of nostalgia changed over time?
It has shifted from being seen as an illness to being seen as beneficial.
It has shifted from being praised to being condemned.
It was once thought to affect only children.
It was once considered rare but is now universal among soldiers.
首句说怀旧曾被视为疾病，后文说现代心理学认为它有积极作用。

Beneath thousands of meters of water lie vast fields of potato-sized nodules rich in cobalt, nickel and manganese—metals essential for electric-vehicle batteries. Mining companies argue that harvesting them would cause less damage than tearing up rainforests on land. Marine biologists, however, point out that the deep seabed is one of the least explored habitats on Earth, home to species found nowhere else. Since ecosystems there recover over centuries rather than years, they warn, any damage may be effectively permanent.◆What argument do the mining companies make?
Seabed mining would be less destructive than mining on land.
Deep-sea species can quickly adapt to disturbance.
Electric vehicles no longer require cobalt.
The seabed has already been thoroughly explored.
第二句说采矿公司认为开采海底结核比破坏陆地雨林造成的伤害小。

Open-plan offices were introduced with the promise that removing walls would encourage spontaneous conversation and collaboration. Employees talked face to face less after the move.
Email use declined in the open offices.

Long-term surveys in Europe and North America indicate that insect populations have dropped sharply over the past few decades. Because insects pollinate crops, recycle nutrients and serve as food for birds, their decline could ripple through entire ecosystems. Scientists blame a combination of habitat loss, pesticide use and climate change, though the relative weight of each factor remains disputed. Some researchers also caution that data from the tropics, where most insect species live, are extremely limited, making global estimates uncertain.◆Why is the decline of insects a cause for concern?
Insects perform functions on which whole ecosystems depend.
Insects are a major source of food for humans.
Insects are the main cause of crop failure.
第二句说昆虫授粉、循环养分、为鸟类提供食物，其减少会波及整个生态系统。

When massive open online courses (MOOCs) appeared around 2012, enthusiasts predicted they would democratize higher education by offering lectures from elite universities free to anyone with an internet connection. A decade later, the results are mixed. Completion rates typically hover below 10 percent, and most of those who finish already hold a university degree. Critics conclude that MOOCs have mainly benefited the well-educated, while defenders reply that even partial participation can spark lifelong learning.◆According to the critics, who has benefited most from MOOCs?
People who already hold university degrees.
文中说完成课程者大多已有大学学历，批评者认为慕课主要惠及受过良好教育的人。

In 1993, a short paper reported that students who listened to a Mozart sonata performed slightly better on a spatial reasoning task. The media quickly inflated the finding into a claim that classical music makes babies smarter, and some parents bought CDs specifically for their infants. Later studies found that the effect, where it appeared at all, lasted only about fifteen minutes and could be produced by any music the listener enjoyed. The episode is often cited as a cautionary tale about how scientific results can be distorted on their way to the public.◆What did later studies show?
The effect was brief and not unique to Mozart.
Classical music permanently raised babies' intelligence.
The original study had never been published.
后续研究发现效果只持续约 15 分钟，且听者喜欢的任何音乐都能产生。

The high cost of electricity for lighting.
A shortage of water in cities.
末句明确指出主要障碍是能源：用电灯替代免费阳光成本高昂。

Fact-checkers have long worried about a 'backfire effect', in which correcting a false belief causes people to cling to it even more firmly. Early experiments seemed to confirm this fear, but larger replication studies have found the effect to be rare. In most cases, corrections do shift people's beliefs in the right direction, although the change often fades within weeks. The more pressing problem, researchers now argue, is not that corrections backfire but that they seldom reach the same audience as the original falsehood.◆What have larger replication studies found about the backfire effect?
It is stronger than first thought.
It is caused by fact-checkers' own bias.
第二句说规模更大的重复研究发现这种效应很少出现。

Despite the convenience of tablets and e-readers, a number of studies suggest that people understand long, complex texts slightly better when reading on paper. The gap is small for simple narratives but larger for informational texts read under time pressure. One explanation is that readers on screens tend to skim, overestimating how much they have understood. Interestingly, the disadvantage shrinks when readers are explicitly told to slow down, implying that habits rather than the screen itself are to blame.◆When is the gap between paper and screen reading largest?
When informational texts are read under time pressure.
When simple stories are read slowly.
When short texts are read for pleasure.
When texts are read aloud to children.
第二句说对简单叙事差距小，而在时间压力下阅读说明性文本时差距较大。

Cities such as Venice and Barcelona have become victims of their own popularity. Cruise ships unload thousands of day-trippers who crowd narrow streets but spend relatively little money locally. Meanwhile, short-term rental platforms have pushed up housing costs, driving long-time residents out of historic centers. In response, Venice introduced an entry fee for day visitors, a measure critics dismissed as turning the city into a theme park, while supporters saw it as a necessary step to protect its fragile infrastructure.◆What problem do short-term rental platforms cause?
They raise housing costs and push out residents.
They reduce the number of cruise ships.
They make tourists spend less money.
第三句说短租平台推高房价，迫使老居民搬离历史城区。

Boredom is usually seen as something to be avoided, and smartphones have made it easier than ever to fill every spare moment. Yet psychologists suggest that boredom may serve a purpose. In one experiment, participants who first completed a dull task—copying numbers from a telephone directory—later came up with more creative uses for everyday objects than those who had not. Boredom, the researchers propose, pushes the mind to wander and seek new stimulation, which can lead to original ideas.◆What did the experiment show?
People who did a boring task were more creative afterwards.
Smartphone users were more creative than others.
实验中先做枯燥任务的人随后想出了更多富有创意的物品用途。

In 2015 China launched its 'sponge city' initiative to tackle the urban flooding that often follows heavy summer rains. Instead of channeling rainwater away as quickly as possible through concrete drains, sponge cities aim to absorb, store and reuse it. Permeable pavements, rooftop gardens and restored wetlands allow water to soak into the ground, reducing pressure on drainage systems. Experts note, however, that such designs work best for moderate rainfall and cannot by themselves cope with the extreme downpours that climate change is making more frequent.◆How do sponge cities differ from the traditional approach?
They absorb and reuse rainwater rather than draining it away quickly.
They rely mainly on larger concrete drains.
They prevent rain from falling on urban areas.
They relocate residents away from flood zones.
第二句说海绵城市不是尽快用混凝土管道排走雨水，而是吸收、储存和再利用。

Gene-editing tools such as CRISPR allow scientists to make precise changes to a plant's own DNA without inserting genes from other species. Supporters argue that this distinguishes gene-edited crops from earlier genetically modified organisms and that they should therefore face lighter regulation. Several countries have agreed, while the European Union long treated them much like conventional GMOs. Critics worry less about safety than about corporate control, fearing that patents on edited seeds could concentrate power in the hands of a few large firms.◆Why do supporters believe gene-edited crops deserve lighter regulation?
They involve changes to the plant's own DNA rather than foreign genes.
They have been grown by farmers for centuries.
They are cheaper than conventional seeds.
支持者认为基因编辑只改变植物自身 DNA、不插入外来基因，与传统转基因不同，因此应放宽监管。

With one of the world's oldest populations, Japan has invested heavily in robots designed to assist in elderly care, from machines that help lift patients out of bed to seal-shaped companions that respond to touch. Yet surveys of care homes reveal that relatively few of these devices are in regular use. Staff complain that the robots are costly, time-consuming to set up and sometimes create more work than they save. The experience suggests that technology alone cannot solve labor shortages unless it is designed around the realities of daily care.◆What do the surveys of care homes reveal?
Few care robots are actually used on a regular basis.
Robots have replaced most care workers.
Seal-shaped robots are the most expensive devices.
第二句说调查发现这些设备中经常使用的相对很少。

During the pandemic, many American universities stopped requiring applicants to submit standardized test scores, hoping to widen access for disadvantaged students. Several prestigious institutions have since reinstated the requirement. Their internal research found that test scores predicted academic success better than high school grades, which have become inflated. More surprisingly, they argued that dropping tests had actually hurt some low-income applicants, whose strong scores could have signaled talents that their under-resourced schools failed to reveal.◆Why did some universities reinstate the test requirement?
Scores proved better predictors of academic success than grades.
Students demanded that the tests return.
High school grades were unavailable after the pandemic.
Tests were cheaper to administer than interviews.
第三句说内部研究发现考试成绩比高中成绩更能预测学业表现。

Artificial light at night has transformed modern life, but it comes at an ecological cost. Newly hatched sea turtles, which instinctively crawl toward the brightest horizon, are lured inland by beachfront lights instead of heading to the sea. Migrating birds collide with illuminated skyscrapers by the millions each year. Unlike many forms of pollution, however, light pollution can be reversed almost instantly: shielding fixtures, dimming lights and switching them off when not needed can bring back dark skies overnight.◆Why do newly hatched sea turtles move inland?
They mistake artificial lights for the bright horizon over the sea.
They are searching for food on land.
They are frightened by the sound of waves.
They follow the routes of migrating birds.
幼龟本能地爬向最亮的地平线，却被海滩灯光引向内陆。

The murals in the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang, painted over the course of a thousand years, are threatened by humidity, drifting sand and the breath of visitors. To protect them, conservators have spent decades creating high-resolution digital copies of the caves. Visitors now watch immersive films and explore virtual caves before entering a limited number of real ones for a shorter time. Officials say the approach balances access with preservation, though some visitors feel that no reproduction can replace the experience of standing before the original.◆Which of the following is mentioned as a threat to the murals?
首句提到湿度、风沙和游客呼吸是壁画面临的威胁；其他选项文中未提。
